name: Lyndon B. Johnson
summary: A New Deal Democrat who, as Senate leader and president, expanded federal programs against poverty and for health care, schooling and civil rights, and signed consumer, gun and crime laws, while keeping a large military, the draft and an escalating war in Vietnam. In Congress he had voted against early civil rights bills and for Taft-Hartley, the 1950 Internal Security Act and the 1954 ban on the Communist Party, then drove the 1957 and 1960 civil rights acts and signed the 1964, 1965 and 1968 laws.

reviewHistory.rationale: He signed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution authorising force to assist allies in Southeast Asia, not only to defend the United States, though the war began with a reported attack on US ships.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

future-generations.rationale: Called for a conservation effort to leave 'a green legacy for tomorrow' and warned that destroyed natural splendour can never be recaptured.

arms-reduction.rationale: Listed controlling, reducing and 'ultimately eliminating' the engines of destruction as a principle of policy and worked on non-proliferation, while raising military spending for Vietnam.

capital-controls.rationale: He signed the Interest Equalization Tax Act of 1964, which taxed Americans' purchases of foreign securities to curb the outflow of capital.

public-service-media.rationale: He signed the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967, which created a federally funded nonprofit corporation, not a government agency, to protect public broadcasting "from extraneous interference and control".

reviewHistory.rationale: Signed the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967 to create non-commercial educational television.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: He voted for the Taft-Hartley Act in 1947 and to override Truman's veto, and in 1949 against striking the clause giving state laws on union shops precedence; his 1966 request to repeal section 14(b) is words and is left out.

reviewHistory.rationale: Asked Congress to repeal section 14(b) of Taft-Hartley, which lets states ban compulsory union membership, to equalise labor laws with the states that have no right-to-work measures.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Proposed a 'substantial cut in excise taxes' in 1964 to leave more money with consumers; those were taxes on selected goods and services rather than general sales taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Mixed: the War on Poverty targeted the poor, while Medicare and education aid were broad programs for the elderly or all schools.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Named the heritage of slavery, oppression and 'present prejudice' as a main cause of Black poverty, alongside inherited poverty, and said the gap was widening 'despite the court orders and the laws'.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: He signed the 1965 act ending the national-origins quota system, after voting in 1952 to enact the McCarran-Walter Act over Truman's veto, which retained it.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: He voted for wartime price control in 1941 and in 1950-1952 against amendments removing the Korean War price and wage stabilization titles.

notes: Pass 2 (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-07, rules 4): every source tagged action or words; answers with a record (his House and Senate roll calls 1937-1960 from Voteview, and laws he signed, cited from the Statutes at Large on GovInfo) were re-sourced to the record alone and their earlier word-based versions kept in reviewHistory. no-compulsory-union changed from -2 (his 1966 request to repeal Taft-Hartley 14(b), words) to +1 on his votes for Taft-Hartley and for state union-shop precedence (1947, 1949). Over time: he voted against anti-lynching and anti-poll-tax bills in the House and for a 1950 segregated-units amendment, then supported the 1957 and 1960 acts, the 1960 anti-poll-tax amendment and signed the 1964-68 laws; the later sustained record is used. Themes searched: economy (taxes, wages, labor, price and rent controls, trade, capital), government (term limits, electoral college, treaties, internal security), world (alliances, aid, Vietnam, Dominican Republic), liberty (drugs, prisons, wiretaps, information), society and culture (immigration, language, race), ecology and technology (oil depletion, space, pollution). Searched: Voteview roll calls (all 3,038 of his votes), the Stanford parsed Congressional Record (his floor speeches 1937-1960), the Miller Center speeches, and his signed statutes. A 1958 floor passage defending the oil depletion allowance was left out because it is an inserted statement by another speaker (it refers to '18 years on the Senate Finance Committee'). presidency.ucsb.edu's robots.txt now disallows ClaudeBot, so new presidential texts were taken from the Miller Center corpus and GovInfo instead. Vietnam: he escalated the war after the Tonkin Gulf Resolution (1964) and on March 31, 1968 limited the bombing and said he would not seek reelection.
